t: You're looking at the W. S. Gilbert Memorial, a Grade II listed bronze plaque on the Victoria Embankment. It sits on a granite block beside Hungerford Bridge, alongside the Bazalgette Memorial. It remembers Sir William Schwenck Gilbert, the dramatist and librettist best known for his collaboration with the composer Arthur Sullivan. Together they produced fourteen comic operas, among them H.M.S. Pinafore, The Pirates of Penzance and The Mikado. The plaque was made by the sculptor Sir George Frampton, whose Edith Cavell Memorial in London and Peter Pan statue in Kensington Gardens are probably his best known works.
